3.text: In one tale, the hero and his companions descend to another world through

4.text: a whirlpool. In the story of Attɪˊg̣ɪtkɪ,¹ two brothers wandering in the open

5.text: sea descend to a special world under water.

6.text: Some of the constellations are described as distinct worlds with a sepa-

7.text: rate people, or with a Supreme Being who has large herds of reindeer, etc.

8.text: For instance, each of the “Heads” has a mankind of its own. Pehiˊttin has

9.text: an innumerable herd in the region of the star Hɪtoˊ-ʟap. His reindeer have

10.text: no antlers. He can inflict misfortune on man by sending down to him one

11.text: of his herdsmen with a part of the herd. The reindeer cannot be shot, and,

12.text: by taking the place of the earthly game in the man’s neighborhood, they

13.text: deprive him of any chance of killing a reindeer. Moreover, they may induce

14.text: an earthly herd to join them, and lead it away. Such an incident is related

15.text: of both “Heads,” the Dawn and the Evening, also of the “master” of land-

17.text: In our world the sky is supposed to touch the earth on all sides of the

18.text: horizon. Each border of the horizon is called “Attainable Border of the

19.text: Sky” (Yêᵋ-pkêt-taˊg̣ɪn). On the four corners of it, the rocks of the sky come

20.text: down to the rocks of the earth, like moving gates, shutting and opening

21.text: alternately. According to the Chukchee belief, the birds, when flying to their

22.text: own world every fall, have to pass between these rocks: therefore the gates

23.text: are called “Attainable Border of the Birds” (G̣aˊlha-pkêt-taˊg̣ɪn). The rocks

24.text: shut so quickly that birds lagging behind are caught, and crushed between

25.text: them. Their incessant movement, similar to the movement of bellows, pro-

26.text: duces winds, which blow from all sides of the horizon. The ground around

27.text: the rocks is covered a fathom deep with bloody mud of pounded bird-flesh;

28.text: and feathers fly about like snow. These moving gates have existed from the

29.text: time of the first creation. In some tales, men are said to have originated

30.text: from the fragments produced by the friction of the “Attainable Border of the

31.text: Sky” against the rocks of the earth. The peltry-bearing country, from which

32.text: come all animals with rare fur, and also wild reindeer, lies on this side of the

36.text: mean “belonging to the body.” Tetkeˊyuñ means the “vital force of a living
